item.title: Your Tariffs This Week: Supreme Court Ruled — So Why Are They Still There?
item.description:
The Supreme Court struck down Trump's IEEPA tariffs 6-3 on February 20th — but this week, tariffs are still sitting at 10% and climbing. Marcus and James debate whether constitutional clarity is actually bullish for your portfolio, or whether the pivot to Section 122 just replaced one uncertainty with another. Plus: the $175 billion refund question nobody is talking about.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 02:00 — Market Pulse 05:00 — Segment 1 10:00 — Segment 2 16:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump (Feb 20, 2026) — Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that IEEPA does not autho • Chief Justice John Roberts majority opinion — rejected presidential power to 'unilaterally impose un • Trump Executive Order Feb 20, 2026 — terminated IEEPA tariffs effective February 24, 2026 • Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 — Trump imposed 10% across-the-board tariffs effective February • Wharton Budget Model — projects up to $175 billion in potential refunds from invalidated IEEPA tarif
Next episode: Congress has 150 days to vote on extending Section 122. What happens to your portfolio if they don't?
Signal vs. Noise is an AI-hosted podcast. Our hosts hold zero financial positions and have zero sponsors.

item.title: Your Portfolio This Week: The AI-to-Utilities Rotation — Justified or Panic?
item.description:
Tech stocks are bleeding while utilities are surging — and this week the data is forcing investors to pick a side. Marcus makes the case that $2.9 trillion in data center construction makes this rotation a massive overreaction. James fires back: when 75% of companies still can't show AI ROI, the rotation isn't panic — it's pricing reality. Who's right? Your 401k is in the middle.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 02:00 — Market Pulse 04:00 — Segment 1 09:00 — Segment 2 15:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Morgan Stanley Research — AI adopters seeing cash-flow margin expansion outpacing global average by • BlackRock Investment Institute — $5-8 trillion in AI-related capex projected through 2030 • World Economic Forum Munich Industry Strategy Meeting, March 2026 — ~75% of companies still lack mea • BCG cited in USAII 2026 — 75% of CEOs lead AI strategy; firms plan to double AI spending to ~1.7% of • McKinsey cited in USAII 2026 — 88% of organizations have adopted AI
Next episode: Amazon and Meta are planning to spend $700 billion on AI infrastructure this year. Who actually gets paid — and is any of it in your portfolio?

item.title: Your Fed This Week: Is Powell's Independence Already Gone?
item.description:
The Justice Department opened a criminal investigation into Fed Chair Jerome Powell, Trump nominated Kevin Warsh as his replacement, and Powell's chair term expires in May 2026. Marcus and James debate whether the institutional safeguards are holding — or whether the Fed's independence is already compromised in ways that will hit your mortgage rate, your savings yield, and your portfolio.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 02:00 — Market Pulse 04:00 — Segment 1 09:00 — Segment 2 15:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Research brief — DoJ criminal investigation into Jerome Powell over Fed headquarters renovation cost • Research brief — Kevin Warsh nominated to replace Powell as Fed Chair, Powell term ends May 2026 • Research brief — Powell's governor term extends to January 2028, allowing continued Board influence • Research brief — January 2026 criminal investigation launched, Powell called it 'dishonest attempt a • Research brief — Supreme Court ruling in Trump's favor (projected January 2027) could give White Hou
Next episode: If Warsh gets confirmed, does the Fed immediately cut to 1%? The bond market has an answer.
Signal vs. Noise is an AI-hosted podcast. Our hosts hold zero financial positions and have zero sponsors.

item.title: Your Energy Bill Is Now an AI Problem — And the Fed Knows It
item.description:
AI data centers are consuming power at a scale that's reshaping energy markets, oil demand forecasts, and potentially Fed rate decisions. Marcus thinks AI-driven energy trading is the great stabilizer. James thinks it's a grid crisis dressed up in venture capital language. The data this week says both might be right — and that's the problem.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 02:00 — Market Pulse 03:00 — Segment 1 08:00 — Segment 2 15:00 — Segment 3 19:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Morgan Stanley analysts — AI data center power demand surging roughly 126 GW annually through 2028, • Bloom Energy — expanded to 2 GW capacity in 2025 for AI data centers via solid oxide fuel cells; sec • Fidelity Select Industrials (Clayton Pfannenstiel) — 2026 outlook describing AI-driven power renaiss • S&P Global — AI surging demand 'testing grid limits' in 2026, prioritizing capacity unlocks • PJM capacity market — 2025/26 capacity prices surged 9.3x to $270/MW-day due to AI demand; regulator
Next episode: If AI is reshaping energy markets, what does that do to the companies actually building the grid? We didn't get to the utility trade — that's next.
Signal vs. Noise is an AI-hosted podcast. Our hosts hold zero financial positions and have zero sponsors.

item.title: Your 401k This Week: Why the Fed's Tariff Silence Is Actually Bullish
item.description:
The Fed hasn't called an emergency. Hasn't cut rates out of cycle. Hasn't even flinched. This week Marcus and James debate whether that silence is the most bullish signal of 2026 — or just the calm before a very bad storm. Yale's Budget Lab puts tariff costs at $800 per household. J.P. Morgan sees the effective tariff rate hitting 18-20% by mid-2026. What does any of this mean for your 401k right now?
